description: We are a group of students from senior year on a Brazilian high school. We are united to change people's vision on how Earth can be studied.
summary:
Terra Sonora is an "Earth Jukebox" that turns NASA satellite data into music you hear live. It runs in any web browser. Users explore a hand-painted globe, tap any place on Earth and hear it. The app plays 27 data channels at once: temperature, wind, rain, vegetation, soil moisture, fires and more. They come from MERRA-2, POWER, MODIS, SMAP, GPM, GRACE and FIRMS. The sound is made on the spot in the browser. The matching EIC/VEDA or GIBS satellite image appears on the map while the sound plays, so what you see and what you hear come from the same data. Each place is compared with the 1991–2020 climate average, and unusual months are flagged.
Extra layers show wind, cyclones, tornadoes, tsunamis, volcanoes, live earthquakes, animal migration routes, tectonic plates and the day/night line. Study Mode plays long pieces in 12 music styles shaped by the data. Satellite Ear is a game for guessing places by ear: players listen to a spot on Earth and drop a pin where they think it is. It has daily challenges, a world ranking and rooms to play with friends. Terra Sonora works without sight and comes in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) API: MERRA-2 and CERES monthly/daily point data
NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services) WMTS imagery
NASA FIRMS active fires, VIIRS 375 m (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21)
MERRA-2 reanalysis (NASA GMAO, via GES DISC OPeNDAP)
AIRS L3 Monthly v7 (AIRS3STM): ozone, CO, CH₄ (NASA GES DISC)
